target: Deadline-nya besok, tapi laporan saya sudah selesai hari ini.
english: The deadline is tomorrow, but my report is already finished today.
tip: -nya can mean 'the one we know': deadline-nya besok = the deadline is tomorrow.

target: Waktu kita tinggal dua hari sebelum deadline proyek.
english: We only have two days left before the project deadline.
tip: tinggal usually means live or stay, but here it means 'remaining': waktu kita tinggal dua hari = we only have two days left. Context decides which tinggal you've met.

target: Bu Rina, mohon maaf, laporan saya terlambat satu hari.
english: Mrs. Rina, my apologies, my report is one day late.
tip: mohon maaf = formal apology, softer than plain maaf: Mohon maaf, Bu, saya terlambat.

target: Kalau mau cuti panjang, ajukan jauh-jauh hari.
english: If you want a long leave, put in for it well in advance.
tip: jauh-jauh hari is literally 'far-far days' – doubling jauh stretches the distance in time, giving 'well in advance': ajukan jauh-jauh hari.

target: Pak Dedi, saya mohon izin cuti hari Jumat.
english: Mr. Dedi, I would like to request leave on Friday.
tip: mohon izin = formal 'I request permission': saya mohon izin cuti = I request leave.

target: Selama saya cuti, Rina yang menggantikan saya.
english: While I'm on leave, Rina is the one covering for me.
tip: yang marks who does it: Rina yang menggantikan saya = it's Rina who covers for me.

target: Cuti bersama tahun ini jatuh pada bulan Desember.
english: This year's collective leave falls in December.
tip: cuti bersama = collective leave the whole office takes at once: cuti bersama bulan Desember.

target: Halo Bu, saya tidak bisa masuk hari ini karena demam.
english: Hello ma'am, I can't come in today because I have a fever.
tip: masuk literally means enter, but by itself it means coming in to work or school: saya tidak bisa masuk = I can't come in. tidak masuk is the standard 'absent'.

target: Kalau badan tidak enak, jangan paksakan diri bekerja.
english: If you're feeling unwell, don't force yourself to work.
tip: badan tidak enak = feeling unwell (lit. body not nice): kalau badan tidak enak, istirahat.

target: Saya melamar kerja di perusahaan teknologi di Jakarta.
english: I applied for a job at a technology company in Jakarta.
tip: melamar kerja = to apply for a job — melamar alone can also mean to propose marriage!

target: Ceritakan pengalaman kerja Anda di perusahaan sebelumnya.
english: Tell me about your work experience at your previous company.
tip: Interviewers use Anda, never kamu: pengalaman kerja Anda = your work experience.

target: Gaji di sini lebih tinggi, tapi kerjanya juga berat.
english: The salary here is higher, but the work is also heavy.
tip: Bare kerja is any work; add -nya and it's this specific one: kerjanya juga berat = the work is also heavy. -nya often does the job of English 'the'.

target: Saya masih pikir-pikir soal tawaran itu.
english: I'm still thinking over that offer.
tip: Doubling a verb softens it: pikir-pikir = mull it over for a while.

target: Bu Maya, terima kasih atas kesempatan wawancara ini.
english: Mrs. Maya, thank you for this interview opportunity.
tip: In thanks, atas = for: terima kasih atas kesempatan ini = thank you for this opportunity.

target: Kalau kamu sibuk, biar saya yang balas email klien.
english: If you're busy, let me be the one to reply to the client's email.
tip: biar saya yang... = let me be the one to...: biar saya yang balas = let me reply.

target: Jangan sungkan bertanya kalau ada yang belum jelas.
english: Don't hesitate to ask if anything isn't clear yet.
tip: Sungkan isn't plain hesitation – it's the feeling of not wanting to impose on someone. Jangan sungkan bertanya = don't hold back out of politeness, just ask.

target: Kami saling membantu supaya pekerjaan cepat selesai.
english: We help each other so the work gets finished quickly.
tip: Saling before a verb makes it mutual: membantu = help, saling membantu = help each other. No extra 'each other' word needed after the verb.

target: Dia meminjamkan payungnya ke saya waktu hujan deras.
english: She lent me her umbrella when it was raining hard.
tip: pinjam = borrow, meminjamkan = lend: dia meminjamkan payungnya = she lent her umbrella.

target: Kalau saya lembur, dia sering membawakan saya kopi.
english: When I work overtime, she often brings me coffee.
tip: -kan can add 'for someone': bawa → membawakan saya kopi = bring me coffee.

target: Pak Tono, boleh saya minta tolong periksa dokumen ini?
english: Mr. Tono, may I ask you to please check this document?
tip: minta tolong = ask a favor: boleh saya minta tolong? = may I ask a favor?

target: Dokumen kontrak ini perlu tanda tangan Pak Direktur.
english: This contract document needs the director's signature.
tip: tanda tangan = signature (lit. hand mark): perlu tanda tangan = needs a signature.

target: Saya salah kirim email ke klien lain.
english: I sent the email to a different client by mistake.
tip: salah + verb = do it wrong: salah kirim = sent to the wrong place.

target: Tolong kirim ulang lampirannya, file tadi tidak bisa dibuka.
english: Please re-send the attachment; the earlier file couldn't be opened.
tip: verb + ulang = do it again: kirim ulang = re-send it.

target: Bu Sinta, mohon periksa dokumen ini sebelum saya kirim ke klien.
english: Mrs. Sinta, please check this document before I send it to the client.
tip: mohon + verb = very polite request, softer than tolong: mohon periksa = please check.

target: Setelah lembur seminggu, akhirnya proyek kami selesai juga.
english: After a week of overtime, our project is finally done.
tip: akhirnya ... juga = finally, at last: akhirnya selesai juga = it's finally done.

target: Kami harus check-in dua jam sebelum pesawat berangkat.
english: We have to check in two hours before the plane departs.
tip: Indonesians use English check-in as-is at airports and hotels: check-in dua jam sebelumnya = check in two hours early.

target: Boleh saya lihat paspor dan tiket Anda?
english: May I see your passport and ticket?
tip: Anda (capital A) is the polite you that staff use with strangers: paspor Anda = your passport.

target: Bagasi saya beratnya dua puluh tiga kilo.
english: My luggage weighs twenty-three kilos.
tip: -nya turns a describing word into a noun: berat = heavy, beratnya = its weight.

target: Tas kecil ini saya bawa ke dalam pesawat saja.
english: This small bag I'll just take into the plane.
tip: Indonesian often puts the object first: Tas kecil ini saya bawa = this small bag I'll take. The doer comes right after it, with no extra words needed.

target: Tolong taruh koper Anda di atas timbangan.
english: Please put your suitcase on the scale.
tip: tolong literally means help, and it turns any command into a polite request: Tolong taruh koper Anda = please put your suitcase.
